audit_scope: Native constructor unchanged. Query inputs and demo answers only reach independent uniqueness gate. Thirty-two collision mechanisms fitted to demos; unresolved query disagreement rejects. 250 episodes, 1000 fresh pairs, all eight D4 and shared random palette.
provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
The emitted program works in visible coordinates and never rotates or recolours a grid.

Scene parsing:
- Divider lines are full rows or columns of palette[0], whichever way D4 laid them out.
- The background is palette[8].
- Each panel contributes its largest 4-connected same-colour component, which is the constructor's own component definition.

Candidate mechanisms. Instead of fixing one collision rule, the program enumerates a family of rules that is closed under D4. It has 32 members:
- Placement order (4 choices): visible panel order forward, visible panel order backward, size descending, size ascending. A size order with ties is defined only if every tie-consistent order gives the same output.
- Collision policy (8 choices). Every policy leaves a piece at shift 0 when its spot is free. On collision it either:
  - overwrites;
  - lets the earlier piece win;
  - takes the unique nearest free shift (Manhattan distance);
  - takes the unique nearest free axis shift;
  - slides in one of the four visible directions until it fits.
- The nearest-shift policies have no tie-break. A tie makes the candidate undefined.

Selection:
- Every candidate is checked against each demonstration's actual output, and inconsistent ones are discarded.
- All survivors are applied to the query and must agree exactly.
- If they disagree, or one is undefined, the program raises an explicit 'not identifiable' error rather than picking a winner.

Fixture episode, hand-derived:
- Pair 1: overwrite and earlier-wins are refuted. The up slide fits only at k=3 and gives the wrong cells. The right and down slides leave the canvas. The asc and backward orders would move the staircase, which the label keeps in place.
- Six candidates survive: {size desc, panel forward} × {nearest, nearest-axis, slide toward canonical-left}. All six reproduce the label.
- Pairs 2–4 are collision-free overlays, so they keep these six.
- Both test queries are collision-free, so all survivors return the plain overlay. That matches the approved labels.

Fresh episodes: kept shapes can never overlap, so every candidate survives and every candidate returns the overlay.
draft_notes.limitations:
- Nothing was executed. All traces above were done by hand.
- If a query's kept shapes collide, its answer is determined only when the surviving rules agree. Otherwise the program raises ValueError by design. This never happens for constructor-reachable queries or for the two approved test queries.
- A tied largest component inside a query panel also raises an error. The constructor rejects such scenes.
- The program assumes dividers are complete lines of palette[0] and that panels are equal-sized. Shape colours never include palette[0] or palette[8].
- d4 is unused on purpose. The rule is D4-equivariant and the candidate family is D4-closed.
- The host's fresh-pair audit cannot exercise collision handling, because the sampler never produces collisions. Collision handling is validated only through demo pair 1 and its D4 and palette variants.
- If the host ever made train pair 1 the query with only collision-free demos, the program would correctly refuse. In that setting, overwrite and slide both survive and disagree.
draft_notes.diagnosis:
The hold asks whether the extra_color fixture branch can be read as a uniform visible mechanism. It can, and here the demonstrations establish that reading rather than an assumption or D4.

(1) A colour-specific rule ('colour 6 moves left') is refuted inside the same episode, under the same palette colour. Colour-6 kept shapes stay in place in pair 2 (panel 1, rows 2–3) and in pair 3 (panel 0 L-shape). The evidence gate reports this as colour_specific_shift_refuted.

(2) A panel-specific rule ('the third panel shifts') is refuted. Third-panel shapes stay in place in pairs 2, 3 and 4.

(3) The only displacement in the episode happens exactly where the plain overlay collides. In pair 1 the 6-shape at (3,2),(3,3),(4,3),(4,4) hits the staircase at (3,3) and (4,4). So the visible trigger is collision.

(4) Among 32 enumerated collision-resolution rules, the demos leave 6 survivors. All of them place the 6-shape at (3,1),(3,2),(4,2),(4,3), and all agree on every collision-free query. No arbitrary first candidate or colour tie-break is used, and D4 decides nothing.

(5) Reachable queries are collision-free. Random scenes draw each cell of one 5×5 union with a single panel index, so kept shapes are disjoint. Both approved tests were checked by hand to be disjoint overlays:
- test 1: 6-T, 1-U, and the row of 4s;
- test 2: 3-shape, 2-zigzag, 5-block. Its size-6 tie across panels is harmless because there is no collision.

Identical-input / different-output witness: generate(colors=PAIR1, extra_color=6) and generate(colors=PAIR1, extra_color=None) yield the same input. Rows 3–4 of their outputs differ: [8,6,6,4,4]/[8,8,6,6,4] versus [8,8,6,6,4]/[8,8,8,6,6]. So pair 1's label is not a function of its input under the constructor; it is fixed only as a demonstration.

Separate ambiguity check: an episode whose demos are all collision-free cannot tell overwrite from slide on a colliding input. The emitted program detects this survivor disagreement and refuses. The independent evidence gate flags any colliding query as non-identifiable.
draft_notes.constructor_issue:
1) extra_color is a fixture-only latent. It applies a colour-keyed column offset of −1 and is used only for train pair 1. The same input with extra_color=None produces a different label, so the label is not determined by the input alone. The visible demos still determine it as collision-triggered relocation. Labels are left unchanged.

2) Indexing defect: the offset writes output[row][col-1]. For an extra-colour cell at col 0, Python's negative indexing would silently wrap the write to column 4. The approved fixture does not hit this, because the 6-shape's minimum column is 2. It needs host review if extra_color is ever reused.

3) Coverage gap: the random sampler (colors=None) can never produce colliding kept shapes. Fresh pairs therefore never exercise the slide. I do not propose adding collision scenes. A colliding fresh query would be determined only if the episode builder guaranteed a demonstration that disambiguates the survivor set. Any change to the constructor should be designed and reviewed by the host.

host_review.explanation: The hypothesis family is systematic: four orders times eight collision policies, closed under D4. No colour/fixture lookup, no native D4 direction, no selection of the first surviving rule. Host fixed silent skipping of ambiguous demos, required nonempty demos, and required three equal panels each with exactly two components. Independent gate uses coordinate dictionaries and exhaustive translations instead of NumPy masks and directed scan.
host_review.audit: 1000 unique fresh native pairs,8000 augmented pair checks,16 canonical fixture variants,zero rejections;18.47s. Six tests pass including informative collisions on newly recoloured pieces, counterfactual overwrite labels changing the same query answer, unresolved collision rejection from collision-free demos, originalfixtures, missing/invalid demos never skipped.
host_review.coverage_limit: Default native sampling never creates collisions because its union cells belong to one panel. Fresh audit validates largest-component extraction and overlay; collision generalization is tested with the preserved canonical collision and independently recoloured explicit scenes. Arbitrary extra_color calls can label identical inputs differently and are not identifiable without sufficient demonstrations.
